Q1.why: A decoder is software run over recorded chip data. It bears on operating qubits, not on making them.

Q2.why: Same as Q1: real-time decoding on TPUs, applied to recorded Willow data.

Q3.why: The circuits ran on Willow, but the AI's output is a circuit: software. Nothing about the processor itself changed.

Q4.why: Encodings evaluated by simulation. About qubits, but nothing built or run.

Q5.why: Experiment designs checked by simulated fidelity; photonic states, not qubit scaling. The model is task-trained, so 'autocorrect++' is a stretch here.

X1.why: A standards consequence, not a physical one.

M1.why: Compounds were synthesized from GNoME targets, so AI touched matter. Whether the predictions were necessary is the contested point: Cheetham & Seshadri found mostly compositional variants a conventional screen could reach.

M2.why: A real electrolyte in a prototype cell. AI did the first screen of 32 million; HPC filtering and chemists did the rest, so necessity is arguable.

M3.why: A diffusion model designed the structure to a target property and it was made. One compound: a demonstration, not a leap.

M4.why: An AI-proposed circuit is in silicon. A circuit change in a TPU is an early sign, not a leap in physical engineering; the force-field and lithography figures are software speedups.

M5.why: The proposer chose every cycle's compositions and 2,942 catalysts were made and tested. The closest thing on this page to James's picture, and still a lab result with the company's own comparison.

M6.why: An LLM wrote the recipes and three unreported compounds were made, so AI touched matter. Necessity is arguable: DFT chose the targets, humans ran every step and fed results back, and the paper claims fewer trials, not a route a chemist could not have found.

P1.why: A learned controller held real plasma in shapes the machine had not produced before. Control engineering, not a new material; James named engineering too.

P2.why: Forecasts, deployed and used, but prediction rather than physical engineering.

P3.why: New physics about matter, confirmed by experiment. Knowledge, not engineering; James's bar was a leap in engineering.

P6.why: Theory. This is the result James answered with 'I rest my case'.

P7.why: A record computation in a toy model.

P8.why: Mathematics about an equation of physics; says nothing about real fluids.
